full_judgment:
6. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Senior Advocate along with Mr. SM Arif, Mr. Kazi Mohammad Joynal Abedin and Ms. Smrity B. Usha appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the opposite party Nos. 1-4 in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Case No. 82 of 1985 by filing a joint written objection categorically pleaded that the pre-emption case is bad for defect of parties as all the co-sharers in the khatian were not made parties and substituted opposite party No. 4(Ka) by filing a separate written objection on 11-9-1997 made specific averment to the said effect by mentioning the names of all the co-sharers of the disputed land, therefore, the pre-emption case is hopelessly bad for defect of parties. 

 9. He next submits that if the co-sharers in the khatian are not made parties, the pre-emption case under section 96 of the SAT Act will be bad for defect of parties. In support of his contentions, he has referred a plethora of judgment reported in the Cases of Indrajit Kunda and others vs Bijoy Krishna Kunda being dead his heirs Biswajit Kunda and others reported in 7 BLT (AD) (1999) 386 (Para.-12) : 5 BLC (AD) 429 and Sree Biraj Mohan Roy vs Binodini Roy and others reported in 12 BLT (AD) (2004) 111 (Para.-6), Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan (Md.) and others vs Galman Begum and others reported in 64 DLR (AD) (2012) 133 (Para.9-11), Binodini Dasi vs Mati Lai Sikdar and others reported in 21 DLR (HC) (1969) 262 (Para. 6-7), Anwarul Huq vs irqbal Ahmed and others reported in 11 ADC (2014) 181 (Para. 121), Lai Miah (Hajee) vs Nurul Amin and others reported in 57 DLR (AD) (2005) 65 (Para. 18-19), Ranjit Sarker and others vs Sree Sukhendu Bikash Biswas and others reported in 17 BLD (AD) (1997) 58 (Para. 12) : 2 BLC (AD) 100 and Jahanara Begum and others vs Md. Aminul Islam Chowdhury and others reported in 17 BLD (AD) (1997) 195 (Para. 7): 50 DLR (AD) 52. 

 15. He further submits that there were no other co-sharers in the khatian to be impleaded as opposite parties other than seller and purchaser and moreover, the application for addition of parties was redundant, therefore, it cannot be held that the pre-emption case is bad for defect of parties. He relying upon the facts and circumstances of the case, evidences on record and findings of the Appellate Court submits that there is no other co-sharer in the case khatian to be impleaded as the opposite parties other than seller and, as such, the pre-emption case not bad for defect of parties and there being no finding as to defect of parties, pursuant to the application dated 10-2-2010 for addition of parties and application dated 18-1-2011 for the amendment of the plaint, mere filing of those applications will not come as an aid to arrive any finding of defect of parties unless the defect of parties is apparent on the face of the record. 

 19. The learned Senior Assistant Judge dismissed the pre-emption case mainly on the ground that the pre-emption case is bad for defect of parties. The Appellate Court after delving into the facts and law and considering the evidence on record held that since the pre-emptee-opposite party purchased the case land only mentioning RS Plot of the case holding and all the sharers of the RS Record were made parties. Therefore, the record owners of the BS Survey are not required to be made parties. Since at the time of institution of the case, B.S Survey had not been started, the pre-emptee contended that the impugned deed was not aout and outsale deed, but a deed of disclaimer, therefore, the pre-emption case is not maintainable. But the Appellate Court as a last court of fact thoroughly examined the evidence on record rightly held that all the co-sharers of the R.S holding i.e. case holding were made parties, therefore, there is no necessity to implead the co-sharers of the latest khatian which was prepared after institution of the pre-emption case. In the written objection, the pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-4 under paragraph No. 6 stated to the effect: "প্রার্থীকের মোকদ্দমা পক্ষদোষে সম্পূর্ণরুপে অচল।” 

 23. It appears from the record that the pre-emption case started its journey in the year, 1985. The pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-4 filed a written objection on 14-9-1987. In the written objection under paragraph Nos. 6 and 18, they contended that all the co-sharers of the holding were not made parties. The pre-emptor on 13-9-1988 filed an application for interrogatories requesting to supply the names and addresses of the co-sharers of the case holding. On 21-12-1988, the pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-4 answered to the interrogatories without mentioning the names and addresses of any person and thereby the pre-emptees waived their right to defend that the pre-emption case is bad for defect of parties. The opposite party No. 4 along with the pre-emptee-opposite party Nos. 1-3 filed a joint written objection against the pre-emption case on 14-7-1987 and after that, the opposite No. 4, Rabeya Khatun, left this transitory world and after her sad demise, her legal heirs were substituted as opposite party Nos. 4(Ka)-4(Ga) by Order No. 142 dated 31-3-1997. The opposite party No. 4(Ka) entered appearance in the case and by filing another written objection on 11-9-1997 made specific averment therein that all the co-sharers in the khatian were not made parties. Since the pre-emptee No. 4, Rabeya khatun, waived her right to defend as to the issue of joinder of necessary parties. One of the substituted heirs of Rebaya Khatun i.e. the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 4(Ka), Kamal Uddin Khan's further written objection making specific averments to the effect that some persons were not made parties to the pre-emption case is an afterthought attempt to get the pre-emption application dismissed for defect of parties. The substituted legal heirs cannot fill up the lacuna of the original pre-emptee No. 4, Rabeya Khatun. It is a settled principle of law that all objections on the grounds of non-joinder of parties have to be taken at the earliest possible opportunity, if it is not taken shall be deemed, have been waived. It is true that non-joinder of necessary parties in pre-emption case is fatal. The pre-emptee-opposite party has to make clear averments in his pleadings i.e. the written objection that who are necessary parties. Mere general denial or gentleman denial in the written objection shall not if so facto dismiss the pre-emption case on the ground of non-joinder of necessary parties. Since the pre-emptor requested to answer and gave the details of the persons, who are necessary parties, therefore, the defence of the pre-emptees has been struck out to that effect. The consequence of failure of giving answer to the interrogatories has been clearly spelt out under Order 11 Rule 21 of the CPC.
